summary: Encodes and sends TOP video streams over RTSP server, RTMP sender, SRT, or WebRTC workflows.

key_params.name: mode
key_params.note: RTSP server, RTMP sender, SRT, or WebRTC mode

key_params.name: streamname
key_params.note: Stream path/name for RTSP server mode

key_params.name: multicast
key_params.note: Use multicast UDP packets for RTSP server mode

key_params.name: videocodec
key_params.note: Video codec: H.264, H.265/HEVC, or AV1 where supported

key_params.name: audiochop
key_params.note: Time-sliced audio source sent with video

key_params.name: includesilentaudio
key_params.note: Include silent audio automatically, on, or off

common_gotchas: Video Stream Out TOP requires Windows and an NVIDIA GPU because it uses the NVIDIA hardware encoder.
Mode changes the meaning of URL, port, and stream name parameters.
RTSP can serve multiple clients and share a port across nodes only when stream names differ.
RTSP output does not send directly to another RTSP server via RTP.
GeForce cards have an 8 encoder-session per-system limit.
Streaming services often prefer constant bitrate modes.
Audio CHOP should be timesliced and may need resampling to 44100 or 48000 Hz depending on protocol/codec.
Per-frame metadata can be received by Video Stream In using Info CHOP/DAT.
WebRTC output requires a configured WebRTC DAT with available output tracks.
Windows Firewall can block incoming connections.
key_concepts: Video Stream Out TOP sends compressed video through RTSP server, RTMP sender, SRT, or WebRTC modes.
The operator uses NVIDIA hardware encoding on Windows, with H.264, H.265/HEVC, and AV1 support depending on protocol and GPU.
RTSP mode can serve multiple clients and multiple TOPs can share a port when stream names are unique.
SRT can send per-frame CHOP or DAT metadata in sync with video, while WebRTC requires a WebRTC DAT and selected tracks.
